title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
english: The body is formed gradually, with veins and arteries developing, along with marrow, membranes, and hairs.
The body is constructed slowly, with each limb being formed by the power of the word.
Just as a horse is formed from various components, the dead man, awakened by the voice of the master, is called, formed, and appears from the tomb.
The command to Lazarus is clear: 'Lazarus, come out' (John 11:43).
Before saying 'arise', he commands the exit.
First, Lord, raise him, and then, having arisen, command him to run.
The one lying down is still being hastened to run, a remarkable transformation.
Why do you proclaim the exit to the one lying down before the resurrection?

He says, 'Yes, to the one lying down, I command the run, so that I may not, having been occupied with the dead for two things, delay the exit. I say to him: 'Come out', so that he may run more quickly, having taken one deadline for both resurrection and run.'
Immediately, Lazarus jumps out of the tomb, as if he were a guardian rather than a dead man.
Hades below, as it seems, gives back the dead man and cries out in response.
Hades asks who this is who, with his voice, awakens the dead from their tombs as if they were sleeping.
Hades asks who loosens the old laws of the dead.
Hades is provoked to raise his dead.
Hades asks who proclaims a return to the dead.
Hades sees his scepter of tyranny over humans being taken away, as he sees.
Hades acknowledges that his prison of death is rotten.
Hades recalls that Elijah took one of his dead away for the sake of a woman (1 Kings 17:22-24).
Hades notes that after Elijah, Elisha came and also snatched away some of his dead (2 Kings 4:32-37).
Hades finds that this one is more bitter to him than the dead, having campaigned as a helper, calling the dead who have been buried as if they were living.
Hades has been robbed of a dead person whom he had buried.
The four-day-old body triumphs over Hades, with the funeral clothes dancing together with the living.
Hades fears that he will be trampled afterwards, with the swaddling clothes of the dead person who has escaped alongside him.
Hades wonders who will frighten him, now that he has been conquered by the dead person and has become like a guardian of the dead.
Hades sees Lazarus as a kind of deposit of the tomb, like gold given with seals.
Lazarus was bound with bands and placed with the tomb, but with the same bonds, he was given back to life.
The Jewish crowd was unbelieving and doubtful towards the great wonder-working, even now…
The passage begins and ends mid-sentence, with the original text being a fragment.

title: Resurrection and Envy
english: …As with the blind man who was healed at one time; 'This is he, he is not' (John 9:25).

Just as one intending to return a deposit observes the seals of the deposit so that the sight of the seals might convince the recipient, so Christ the Lord, returning Lazarus to the Jews, used the burial clothes as signs like certain seals for the four-day deposit among the dead, so that those loosening him might see that it was not simply someone else, but he himself whom they had buried.

But the hardness of unbelief remained uncorrected; for having known the dead man, they envied the miracle and were plotting evil intentions; for they said, 'Let them also kill Lazarus, because many among the Jews believed in Jesus because of him' (John 11:47-53).
Oh, the wickedness of the plot!
Is it true, O priests, what happened, or is it a lie?
If it is indeed true, why do you plot to slay the one who is able to rise again?
If the miracle is a fabrication, you are being overly curious about the height of the miracle.
If what happened is a rumor, let him who is falsely rumored to have been raised live more, so that all approaching the living might learn that he was not raised from the dead.
If you slay this man, you help the rumor by destroying the reputation, as the plot is double in both respects.
Oh, the agonizing disease!
The cure for those who envy is the wounding of the envious; the benefactor is envied like the one who harms; the savior is seen as an enemy like the one who kills.
It was right not to grieve at the rising of the dead.
A dead man rose; I shall take the occasion for joy, finding a doctor who has applied a plaster to the dead.
Prepare yourself, human, for the solution to the things distressing you.
Is a child of yours ill? Call upon the one who raised the dead against the disease.
Does a demon trouble the child? The remedy for the suffering is at hand.
Is a servant of yours at the point of death? You have near you the one who draws the dead away from death.
How many gifts have you given, seeking to find a helper in sorrowful things? You have found this one without payment, yet you close your eyes to the discovery.

Since you are fond of gain, allow those who are willing to have the profit, and permit Lazarus to live, lest you become more bitter to people than death, from which he released them, driving them away, lest you make coexisting with you more hopeless than a tomb.
The dead person had hope of life in the tomb and, not even being harmed by the burial clothes, came to life; but to you, living together…

title: Final Judgment
english: The gift of eternal life is in danger of being lost in the tomb, where the body lies lifeless. However, the story of the Jews' wickedness reminds me of Lazarus' resurrection, which in turn reminds me of the resurrection of the dead, when the tombs will be shaken and the dead will rise incorruptible. At that time, the earth will be troubled with fear, and the heavenly trumpets will sound to the people, signaling the start of the final judgment.

The judge will come down from heaven, accompanied by the armies of angels, and the righteous will meet him in the clouds. The demons will be led to judgment, and the devil will be brought bound, while the tyrants will be dragged to the fearful tribunal. The plunder of the rich will be punished, and the patience of the poor will be crowned. The conspiracies of kings will be confessed, and the lives of priests will be examined. The ranks of virgins will be honored, and the hidden adulteries will be punished. The dignity of the sober will be rewarded, and the licentiousness of the adulterers will be punished. The kindness of the long-suffering will be crowned, and the denunciation of the slanderers will be hidden. The crowds of those who have truly repented will be blessed, and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will be scourged. As the apostle Paul says, we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and each will receive what they have done in the body, whether good or evil. Therefore, being reminded of these things, let the lover of pleasure mourn, for matter is the fuel of the fire of hell. Let the luxurious one punish his belly, for it is the source of many evils.

The prophet rebuked the Sodomites for their gluttony, which is a burdensome thing, and he declared that their sin was that they had an abundance of bread and lived in luxury. The rich are warned to hate greed, just as they would hate a reed that fuels unquenchable fire. On the other hand, the poor are encouraged to be strengthened in endurance, for patience is a pious cooling of hell.

The Greek is urged to learn from impiety, and the heretic is warned to search out heretical doctrines as one would search out tombs, before the voice that will shout to the dead comes. This voice is the bridegroom, Christ our God, who will judge the living and the dead. Let us glorify him with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and forever and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
